div.p: The seven-person survey team spent three weeks mapping the tidal delta with a full research permit in hand, recording every transect in careful detail. Progress stayed steady even when the weather turned, and the crew stayed focused on finishing the western channel before the spring tides returned.

Two sonar rigs and a hand-held current meter formed the core kit for the season, backed by a paper logbook that every team member signed at the end of each shift so nothing was lost between rotations.

list.item: Salinity rose sharply above the second channel bend, consistent with the dry-season baseline the team expected going in.
Sediment cores at station four showed three distinct depositional layers, more than any other station sampled this season.

quote.p: The western channel behaves nothing like the model predicted, the lead hydrologist wrote in the shared logbook on the twelfth day of the survey.

div.p: Full instrument logs and the complete depth-by-depth dataset are archived with the department, which calls it the "reference dataset" for anyone who wants to reproduce the transect-by-transect salinity curve described above in full.
Great writeup -- did the sonar rig need recalibration after the storm on day nine?
Station four's layering matches what our own team saw further upstream last spring.
